intended_object: For a commutative ring K and a K-module V with a chosen finite basis indexed by ι, this is the natural isomorphism, over K-algebras R, between the automorphism group functor R ↦ GL_R(V ⊗_K R) (coefficient ring on the right) and the functor of points of the matrix group scheme GL_ι. This is the standard chosen-basis identification GL(V) ≅ GL_n (Milne 2.8). Inferred from the docstring, the module docs and the neighbouring definitions.
explanation: The body composes two existing natural isomorphisms. First, `sourceOrderedGeneralLinearIso` identifies the right-ordered automorphism functor with `generalLinearModuleFunctor` (automorphisms of R ⊗ V) through the swap V ⊗ R ≅ R ⊗ V, applied pointwise and natural in R. Second, `generalLinearModulePointsIso` takes an automorphism of R ⊗ V to its matrix in the base-changed basis 1 ⊗ bᵢ (via `Units.mapEquiv` of `LinearMap.toMatrixAlgEquiv`), which is natural in R by `generalLinearScalarBasis_endBaseChange_matrix`, and then passes from matrix GL to the points of the GL scheme. Both pieces are correct, so the composite is the intended isomorphism GL(V) ≅ GL_n of point functors. The generality is already natural: any commutative base ring, any module with a finite basis (empty bases allowed), and a finite index type with decidable equality, which is needed for matrices. Putting K, V and ι in one universe is bookkeeping so that the functor lives on CommAlgCat K. Mathlib does not appear to have this isomorphism of point functors. The definition is mostly a transport variant of `generalLinearModulePointsIso` for the other tensor order, but it still names a genuine mathematical isomorphism.
